bbq: Dry brines, every rub, finishing. Diamond Crystal dissolves faster than Morton; if a recipe doesn't specify, assume Diamond Crystal.
flavor: Clean and briny. Doesn't add flavor so much as turn up everything else — the single most important ingredient in barbecue.
name: Kosher salt

bbq: Brisket, beef ribs, steaks — anywhere bark matters. Fresh-cracked beats pre-ground every time.
flavor: Sharp, piney heat with a woody bite. The 16-mesh crack is the backbone of Texas-style bark.
name: Coarse black pepper

bbq: Almost every rub. Use powder, not garlic salt, so you control the salt.
flavor: Savory, pungent, faintly sweet when cooked. The workhorse of rubs — deeper than fresh garlic, which can burn.
name: Garlic powder

bbq: Rubs, injections, sauces. Kelly's Ember rubs carry it.
flavor: Sweet-savory depth without the bite of raw onion. Rounds out a rub the way garlic sharpens it.
name: Onion powder

bbq: Rubs where you want color without fire. Chicken and ribs love it.
flavor: Mild, sweet dried pepper. More about color — that deep red mahogany — than heat.
name: Paprika (sweet)

bbq: Rubs, sauces, and anything cooked indoors that wants a whisper of the pit.
flavor: Sweet paprika with real wood-smoke character. Rich, round, faintly bacony.
name: Smoked paprika

bbq: Rubs, sauces, injections. A little goes a long way — 1 tsp per batch is noticeable.
flavor: Clean, straight heat with very little flavor of its own. The dial you turn when a rub needs fire.
name: Cayenne

bbq: Chili, of course, plus beef rubs and beans. Check the label: blends vary wildly.
flavor: A blend — usually ancho, cumin, garlic, oregano. Earthy warmth rather than sharp heat.
name: Chili powder

bbq: Brisket, beef ribs, chili, fajitas. Toast and grind whole seeds if you want the full effect.
flavor: Earthy, nutty, faintly smoky. The 'what is that' note in a lot of great brisket rubs.
name: Cumin

bbq: Brisket rubs, sausage, pickling. Lifts heavy beef.
flavor: Citrusy, floral, almost lemony. Cumin's bright partner — they show up together for a reason.
name: Coriander (ground)

bbq: Sauces (it helps them cling), pork rubs, deviled eggs. Kelly's Ember sauces carry it.
flavor: Sharp, tangy heat that blooms in liquid. Also called mustard flour — same thing, finely ground seed.
name: Dry mustard

bbq: Kelly's Ember pork rub — it's in there. Also coleslaw dressing and pickles.
flavor: Vegetal, faintly bitter, green and savory. A background note you miss when it's gone.
name: Celery seed

bbq: Mustard sauces, rubs where you want gold color. Stains everything — you've been warned.
flavor: Earthy, bitter, faintly peppery. Mostly here for that golden color.
name: Turmeric

bbq: Light-colored sauces, potato salad, white gravy. Anywhere black specks would look wrong.
flavor: Sharp, musty, barnyard-funky heat. Disappears visually — that's the point.
name: White pepper

bbq: Finishing pizzas, pastas, and glazes. Also great in a shaker on the table.
flavor: Chunky, fruity heat with visual punch. Slower burn than cayenne.
name: Red pepper flakes

bbq: Sauces, chili, beef rubs. The mild chile that adds depth without scaring anyone.
flavor: Dried poblano — sweet, raisin-like, faintly smoky. More fruit than fire.
name: Ancho chile

bbq: Sauces, adobo, anything that wants smoke and heat in one move.
flavor: Smoked jalapeño — earthy heat with real smoke character built in.
name: Chipotle

bbq: Jerk seasoning, ham glazes, some rib rubs. A little goes far.
flavor: Tastes like clove, cinnamon, and nutmeg had a baby. Warm and sweet-spicy.
name: Allspice

bbq: Some rib and ham rubs, dessert smokes. Pinch-level doses.
flavor: Sweet warmth, woody and familiar. In BBQ it's a background singer, never the lead.
name: Cinnamon

bbq: Ham, holiday birds. Measure in pinches, not spoons.
flavor: Intensely aromatic, almost numbing. Powerful stuff — easy to overdo.
name: Clove (ground)

bbq: Cream sauces, eggnog-adjacent holiday smokes, some sausage.
flavor: Warm, sweet, faintly piney. Fresh-grated is a different animal than the jar.
name: Nutmeg

bbq: Asian-inspired glazes, some poultry rubs. Fresh ginger for marinades, ground for rubs.
flavor: Sharp, citrusy warmth. Brighter than black pepper, cleaner than cayenne.
name: Ginger (ground)

bbq: Kelly puts 2 tsp in his Ember pork rub (Rod Gray's influence). Try it before you knock it.
flavor: Pure umami — makes meat taste more like itself. No real flavor of its own.
name: MSG

bbq: Kelly's Ember sauce and rub both carry thyme. Beef, lamb, poultry, vegetables — it never fights.
flavor: Earthy, minty, faintly floral. The signature herbal thread in Kelly's cooking.
name: Thyme (dried)

bbq: Beef, lamb, potatoes. Use fresh sprigs on the pit or in the wrap; dried is harsher.
flavor: Piney, resinous, almost camphorous. Potent — a little perfumes a whole cook.
name: Rosemary

bbq: Italian sausage, Mediterranean-style cooks, chimichurri.
flavor: Peppery, bitter, pungent. The pizza herb — stronger dried than fresh.
name: Oregano (dried)

bbq: Poultry, pork, brown butter. Burns bitter over long smokes — add late.
flavor: Earthy, faintly eucalyptus, savory-sweet. Tastes like Thanksgiving.
name: Sage

bbq: Braises, sauces, beans, stocks. Fish it out before serving — nobody eats the leaf.
flavor: Subtle tea-like depth you can't quite name. A background note for long cooks.
name: Bay leaf

bbq: Finishing pizzas, grilled vegetables, fresh sauces. Never in the rub.
flavor: Sweet, clove-like, peppery when fresh. Dies in long heat — this is a finishing herb.
name: Basil (fresh)

bbq: Finishing tacos, grilled fish, fresh salsas. Add off the heat.
flavor: Bright, citrusy, clean — unless you're one of the folks it tastes soapy to. No judgment.
name: Cilantro (fresh)

bbq: Finishing just about anything rich. Chimichurri's backbone.
flavor: Clean, grassy, fresh. The balancer — cuts richness without adding its own agenda.
name: Parsley (flat-leaf)

bbq: Fish, pickles, potato salad, creamy sauces.
flavor: Tangy, faintly anise, fresh-pickle energy.
name: Dill

bbq: Lamb's best friend. Also great in slaws and fresh spring sides.
flavor: Cool, bright, sweet-herbal. A surprise in BBQ, but it works.
name: Mint (fresh)
